title: Which Directions of a Return Journey Remain in Scope for a Tax Return
content:
On an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking carrying a return date, only the unflown directions of the journey may remain in scope when carrier-imposed taxes are returned. What decides it is whether the outbound departure date has already passed.

## The scope

1. Where a return date stands on the booking and the outbound departure date has already passed, only the unflown-direction share of the taxes is in scope: 0.5 of them, which is to say 50 percent.
2. Where a return date stands on the booking and the outbound departure date has not yet passed, the whole of them stays in scope, a share of 1.
3. In every other case no such narrowing of scope is made.

A booking with no return date standing on it never falls on either of the first two conditions, because both open on a return date standing there.

## Judgement table

| Return date on the booking | Outbound departure date | Share in scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | already passed | 0.5 |
| yes | not yet passed | 1 |
| no | either | no such narrowing |

## Hypothetical readings

A one-way Air Ticket Fare Brands booking carries no return date; whatever has become of its outbound, no narrowing of scope is made under this rule.

A return booking whose outbound departed last Tuesday has its outbound direction behind it, so half of the taxes stays in scope. The same booking read a week earlier, with the outbound still ahead, keeps the whole of them in scope.
